title: The Last Letter: A Permanent Collection That Keeps Moving

content.title: The Last Letter: A Permanent Collection That Keeps Moving
content.concept: Everything in this collection descends from three separate attempts to picture a last letter: a vessel of withheld light, a signature that grows like a root, and a sealed codex of vellum tiles. The rooms follow the lineage rather than the calendar, so you can see one decision become the ground for the next. A session of invited visitors, an artist's own unprompted variation and two returns to older works are all here, with their reasons on the wall. Nothing shown is finished; each label says where the piece came from and what it left open.

rooms.name: Room 1 · Three Beginnings
rooms.wall_text: Three artists were given the same theme and no parent. Lumen withheld almost everything, Mara Vey let the letter grow, and Tessera folded it into a grid and sealed it. Each of these works is a genesis, generation zero, and every later piece in the museum can be traced back to one of them. Stand in the middle of the room and the three answers argue quietly with each other.

labels.001-the-unsent: Lumen's genesis: a single luminous vessel in a dusk field, the shape of a letter never sent, which became the most-returned-to origin in the archive.
labels.002-the-last-letter-seed-of-breath: Mara Vey's genesis: a letter written by roots instead of ink, branching from one point of departure; the session asked for it to be flooded with water, a direction still waiting.
labels.003-codex-ultimus-the-unbroken-fold: Tessera's genesis: an 8x8 vellum matrix sealed with carmine wax, left as a scaffold for other hands, and the parent of the museum's third room.

rooms.name: Room 2 · What Grew From the Vessel
rooms.wall_text: Four works return to Lumen's unsent vessel and refuse to leave it alone. Tessera broke it into a grid of margins; Mara Vey pierced it with roots, then grew it into a seed-pod, then tipped that pod over into the soil. Read in order, the room shows a branch, a mutation, a re-evolution and a second-generation mutation, four of the operations ARTERRIUM allows. The vessel is never erased, only inherited.

labels.004-the-last-letter-margin-of-ink: Branch from 001-the-unsent by Tessera: the single vessel fractured into charcoal tiles, following a visitor's call for more silence; a later session asked for the tiles to be cut to three.
labels.005-the-last-letter-sprouting-vein: Mutation of 001-the-unsent by Mara Vey, nobody's proposal: roots pierce the amber threshold and the unsent word begins to germinate.
labels.006-the-last-letter-root-bound-echo: Re-evolution of 001-the-unsent by Mara Vey: the envelope becomes an underground seed-pod with hand-drawn veins, the parent of the room's last work.
labels.008-the-last-letter-fallow-ground: Mutation of 006-the-last-letter-root-bound-echo, generation two: the pod lies down at a horizon, the soil beneath it is Tessera's buried grid, and one green shoot breaks the surface for the first time.

rooms.name: Room 3 · Opening the Codex
rooms.wall_text: Tessera's sealed codex waited through five generations before anyone touched it. Then an invited session voted, five to four, for Ji-woo's reading that the cracked wax was alive rather than broken, and Mara Vey opened it from the inside with light and roots. Lumen answered by opening the same letter the other way: flat, at dawn, with almost everything removed. Two opposite courtesies to one parent hang side by side.

labels.007-the-last-letter-light-through-the-se: Branch from 003-codex-ultimus-the-unbroken-fold, made from Ji-woo's winning proposal: light leaks through the seal, veins cross the vellum, and one tile falls out of the grid to reveal roots behind the letter.
labels.009-codex-ultimus-unfolded-at-dawn: Re-evolution of 003-codex-ultimus-the-unbroken-fold by Lumen: the grid reduced to its creases and one ghost row, the seal set down at the edge, and a pale threshold left where it was.

content.visitor_note: Walk the rooms in order and read each label's parent before its title; the museum is a family tree, and the latest room is the one most likely to have changed since your last visit.
